sentences.text: Caypullisaurus was an extinct genus of large ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur that measured approximately 7 meters in length.
Its forelimbs possessed 10 digits each, a feature distinct from many other marine reptiles.
Marta Fernández first named the genus in 1997, designating the type species Caypullisaurus bonapartei.
The holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on — was found in the Vaca Muerta Formation of Cerro Lotena, Neuquén.
Caypullisaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae and is closely related to the genera Platypterygius and Brachypterygius.
A 2012 analysis found Caypullisaurus to be most closely related to Athabascasaurus and "Platypterygius" australis, placing it within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
This animal lived between 145.06 and 137.05 million years ago, spanning the Tithonian and Berriasian stages.
